speaker: Yi Qi
title: Coordinating Decentralized Supply Chains under Two-Echelon Disruption Risks
abstract:
Supply chain resilience is a crucial topic in supply chain management. Yet, limited attention has been paid to the coordination of decentralized supply chains in which both the supplier and the buyer are exposed to disruption risks. In such settings, coordination is challenging because the entities must align not only operational decisions, but also the deployment of risk mitigation levers. Whether classic coordination contracts remain effective in this context is still not well understood.
This paper studies a two-echelon supply chain consisting of a supplier and a buyer, in which both parties face disruption risks, while the buyer also faces uncertain demand. Risk mitigation inventory, which can be used to mitigate both disruption risks and demand uncertainty, is employed as the risk mitigation lever. Within this setting, we examine several classic coordination contracts, such as price-only contracts, buyback contracts, and buyback contracts with penalty. We show that these simple contracts can fail to achieve coordination under certain conditions, and that such failures cannot be resolved by simply introducing an additional payment parameter.
We then propose two state-contingent contracts to resolve these failures. The first is a scenario-specific pricing contract, where a different price is charged depending on whether a disruption occurs. The second is a purpose-specific pricing contract, where the price of risk mitigation inventory depends on the quantity purchased. We show that both contracts fully coordinate the supply chain while allowing flexible profit allocation between the supplier and the buyer.
